title: Learn Claude Code From Its Creator
headline: The exact setup and workflows from the person who built Claude Code.
subheadline: Learn the practices, configurations, and patterns that Boris Cherny uses every day — parallel sessions, verification loops, custom agents, worktrees, hooks, and the compounding CLAUDE.md flywheel — packaged as a full training with a drop-in setup.
audience: Engineers who want to 2-3x their output with Claude Code
Team leads who want to roll out Claude Code across their org
Operators who want to automate workflows with agents and MCP
Anyone serious about learning Claude Code from the source
outcomes: Run 10-15 parallel Claude sessions like Boris does at Anthropic
Set up verification feedback loops that 2-3x the quality of every output
Build custom agents, commands, and hooks that compound over time
Use git worktrees for fully isolated parallel development
Integrate Slack, BigQuery, Sentry, and other tools via MCP for zero context switching
Deploy a drop-in setup with agents, commands, permissions, and CLAUDE.md into any project

login.title: Member Login
login.subheadline: Enter any email and password to access the full course and setup library.

modules.title: Core Philosophy
modules.headline: The three rules that make everything else work.
modules.subheadline: Boris's approach comes down to three things: always give Claude a verification feedback loop, plan before you execute, and never accept the first answer. This module explains why each one matters and how they compound.
focus: Verification is the #1 lever — feedback loops 2-3x quality
Plan Mode leads to 1-shot implementations, saving hours of iteration
Pushing Claude to do better produces dramatically better results
Opus with thinking mode requires less steering and produces faster end-to-end results
The compounding CLAUDE.md flywheel: every correction prevents all future mistakes

modules.title: Plan Mode
modules.headline: How to get 1-shot implementations instead of iteration hell.
modules.subheadline: Boris starts every complex session in Plan Mode. This module covers the full workflow: enter Plan Mode, iterate on the plan, switch to auto-accept, and how to recover when things go sideways.
focus: Enter Plan Mode with Shift+Tab twice before starting complex tasks
Let Claude ask clarifying questions and answer them thoroughly
Review and iterate on the plan before switching to auto-accept
Recovery pattern: stop, re-enter Plan Mode, analyze, re-plan, resume
Two-Claude pattern: one writes the plan, another reviews it as staff engineer
Name sessions for tracking: claude --name 'auth-refactor'

modules.title: Verification — The #1 Principle
modules.headline: Give Claude a feedback loop and watch quality 2-3x.
modules.subheadline: The single biggest lever for output quality. This module covers every type of verification: test suites, type checking, browser testing, CLI output, and diff verification — plus how to build verification into CLAUDE.md, agents, hooks, and prompts.
focus: Test suites are the strongest verification — bun run test after every change
Type checking catches errors fast — bun run typecheck
Chrome extension lets Claude test frontend UI visually and iterate
Diff verification: 'Prove to me this works — diff behavior on main vs this branch'
Build verification into CLAUDE.md, custom agents, PostToolUse hooks, and prompts
The anti-pattern: letting Claude make changes without any verification

modules.title: CLAUDE.md — The Compounding Flywheel
modules.headline: Every correction prevents all future occurrences of that mistake.
modules.subheadline: Boris maintains a single CLAUDE.md checked into git. The whole team contributes. Every time Claude makes a mistake, they add a correction. Over time, the mistake rate drops measurably. This is compounding engineering.
focus: Single CLAUDE.md checked into git — whole team contributes multiple times weekly
The correction pattern: Claude makes mistake → add to CLAUDE.md → never happens again
GitHub Action with @.claude tags auto-updates CLAUDE.md from PR comments
Notes directory pattern: per-task/project notes that CLAUDE.md points to
Scoping: root-level, subdirectory, and global CLAUDE.md files
What to include: build commands, conventions, corrections. What to skip: obvious advice

modules.title: Parallel Sessions
modules.headline: Running 10-15 Claudes simultaneously is the biggest productivity unlock.
modules.subheadline: Boris runs 5 terminal sessions numbered 1-5, plus 5-10 web sessions, plus phone sessions. System notifications, color-coded tabs, named sessions. This module teaches the dispatch mindset.
focus: 5 terminal sessions in iTerm2 with system notifications for completion
5-10 web sessions on claude.ai for longer-running parallel work
Teleport between devices: claude --teleport moves sessions local↔web↔phone
Session forking: /branch or claude --resume <id> --fork-session
The dispatch mindset: assign task → move to next → come back when pinged
Shell aliases for quick worktree navigation: za, zb, zc

modules.title: Git Worktrees
modules.headline: Parallel isolated development — no clobbering, no conflicts.
modules.subheadline: When running 5+ sessions, they all modify files. Worktrees give each session its own checkout with its own branch. This module covers manual setup, the -w flag, Desktop app checkbox, batch operations, and non-Git VCS support.
focus: claude -w my-feature creates a worktree and starts a session automatically
Desktop app: check the 'worktree' checkbox before starting
Each worktree is a full checkout on its own branch — changes don't affect others
Launch 10 parallel agents with worktree isolation for batch operations
/batch command fans out work to dozens of worktree agents for large migrations
WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for Mercurial, Perforce, and SVN

modules.title: Custom Agents
modules.headline: Build a team of specialized agents in .claude/agents/.
modules.subheadline: Agents are Claude instances with custom system prompts, tool sets, and permissions. Drop a .md file in .claude/agents/ and launch it with --agent. This module covers Boris's agent team and how to build your own.
focus: code-reviewer: spawns 5 parallel subagents checking logic, security, performance, style, edge cases
build-validator: runs typecheck, lint, tests, build in sequence and reports PASS/FAIL
code-simplifier: post-implementation cleanup — dedup, dead code, CLAUDE.md compliance
worktree-worker: isolated worker with 'isolation: worktree' in frontmatter
Agent frontmatter: name, model, description, isolation, permission mode
Subagent pattern: 5 agents explore → 5 more challenge the findings

modules.title: Custom Commands
modules.headline: Slash commands that automate multi-step workflows.
modules.subheadline: Drop a .md file in .claude/commands/ and type /command-name. This module covers Boris's commands: /commit-push-pr, /babysit, /feature-dev, /techdebt, and how to create your own with arguments.
focus: /commit-push-pr: one command to commit, push, and open a PR
/babysit: auto-address code review comments, auto-rebase, shepherd to merge
/feature-dev: Boris's planning-first workflow — spec → plan → review → implement → verify → simplify
/techdebt: find duplicated code and consolidate clear wins
Commands accept $ARGUMENTS: /fix-issue 123 reads the issue and implements a fix
/btw for side queries without interrupting current work

modules.title: Hooks
modules.headline: Deterministic logic that always runs — unlike prompts, which are suggestions.
modules.subheadline: Hooks are shell commands that fire on events: SessionStart, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PermissionRequest, Stop, PostCompact. This module covers Boris's auto-format hook and the full hook event system.
focus: PostToolUse auto-format: bun run format after every Write|Edit — deterministic, not a suggestion
SessionStart: dynamically load context when Claude launches
Stop hook: poke Claude to keep going when it reaches turn end
PostCompact: re-inject critical instructions lost during context compression
PermissionRequest: route permission prompts to Slack/WhatsApp for remote approval
WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove: custom worktree logic for non-Git VCS

modules.title: Permissions & Security
modules.headline: Pre-allow safe commands instead of skipping permissions entirely.
modules.subheadline: Boris pre-allows specific commands like bun run test:* and Edit(/src/**) via /permissions. This module covers the pre-allow pattern, Auto Mode safety classifiers, sandboxing, and when it's appropriate to skip permissions.
focus: Pre-allow pattern: Bash(bun run test:*), Edit(/src/**) — safe commands skip prompts
Wildcard syntax (*) matches any suffix — Bash(gh pr *) covers all gh pr subcommands
Auto Mode: built-in safety classifiers auto-approve safe ops, flag risky ones
Sandboxing: file and network isolation for untrusted or long-running tasks
Sandbox + dontAsk: safe auto-approve because destructive ops blocked at OS level
Enterprise policies: codebase-wide, personal, and org-wide settings layers

modules.title: MCP Integrations
modules.headline: Zero context switching — Slack, BigQuery, Sentry, and more come to you.
modules.subheadline: MCP servers give Claude access to external tools. Boris uses Slack MCP to paste bug threads and say 'fix', BigQuery for natural language analytics, and Sentry for error logs. This module covers setup and the zero-context-switching pattern.
focus: Slack MCP: paste bug thread → 'fix'. Daily summaries. Auto PRs from feedback
BigQuery: 'I haven't written a line of SQL in 6+ months' — natural language queries
Sentry: grab production error logs and stack traces without leaving Claude Code
GitHub Action: @.claude PR integration auto-updates CLAUDE.md
iMessage plugin: text Claude from any Apple device as a Messages contact
MCP config in settings.json: { 'slack': { 'type': 'http', 'url': '...' } }

modules.title: Prompting Techniques
modules.headline: Challenge Claude. Demand proof. Write detailed specs. Use voice.
modules.subheadline: Boris treats Claude like a talented junior engineer — capable of great work, but you need to set the bar high. This module covers his prompting patterns, effort levels, voice input (3x faster than typing), and output styles.
focus: Challenge: 'Grill me on these changes and don't make a PR until I pass your test'
Demand proof: 'Prove this works by diffing behavior on main vs this branch'
Iterative: 'Knowing everything you know now, scrap this and implement the elegant solution'
Voice input is 3x faster than typing — prompts naturally become more detailed
Effort levels: /effort low for quick lookups, /effort max for unlimited reasoning
Output styles: Explanatory, Learning, Custom — set via /config

modules.title: Code Review Automation
modules.headline: Multi-agent review that caught enough bugs to 2x code output per engineer at Anthropic.
modules.subheadline: Boris's code review dispatches 5 subagents in parallel — logic, security, performance, style, edge cases — then 5 more challenge the findings. Only real bugs with file:line references survive. This module covers the full pattern.
focus: First pass: 5 subagents check logic errors, security, performance, style, edge cases
Second pass: 5 subagents challenge every finding — is this actually a bug?
GitHub Action review: runs on every PR, posts inline comments on real bugs
The 'Grill Me' pattern: make Claude test your understanding before allowing a PR
Two-Claude review: one implements, one reviews independently in a separate session
Result: code output per engineer up 200% at Anthropic

modules.title: Long-Running & Scheduled Tasks
modules.headline: Replace cron jobs with Claude-powered automation.
modules.subheadline: /loop runs local recurring tasks up to 3 days. /schedule runs cloud jobs that survive laptop closure. This module covers both, plus Stop hooks, sandboxed auto-approve, and cloud environment setup scripts.
focus: /loop 5m /babysit: auto-address review comments every 5 minutes
/loop 30m /slack-feedback: auto-create PRs from Slack feedback
/schedule daily: cloud-based jobs that run even when your laptop is closed
Stop hook: deterministic check that pokes Claude to continue if not done
Sandboxed auto-approve: --permission-mode=dontAsk in isolated environments
Cloud setup scripts: install deps, configure settings before Claude launches

modules.title: Mobile & Cross-Device
modules.headline: 'When I'm not coding, I'm dispatching.'
modules.subheadline: Claude Code on iOS/Android. Teleport sessions between terminal, web, and phone. Remote control from anywhere. This module covers Boris's cross-device workflow and the dispatch mindset.
focus: Claude Code mobile app: full sessions from your phone (iOS and Android)
Teleport: start in terminal → --teleport to web → continue on phone → teleport back
Remote control: start and manage local sessions from any device
Cowork dispatch: delegate Slack, email, file management from mobile
iMessage integration: text Claude from any Apple device
Session naming and color-coding for easy identification on mobile

modules.title: Team Patterns
modules.headline: Check the setup into git and every new team member gets the full system on clone.
modules.subheadline: Shared CLAUDE.md, shared settings.json, shared agents and commands — all checked into git. This module covers team-scale practices, onboarding, the plugin marketplace concept, and the Slack context dump pattern.
focus: Shared CLAUDE.md: whole team contributes corrections, reviewed like code
Shared settings.json: permissions, hooks, MCP servers — no per-person setup
Shared .claude/agents/ and .claude/commands/: everyone gets the full toolset
Onboarding: clone repo → run install.sh → everything works
Plugin marketplace: teams publish best agents/commands for cross-org adoption
Slack sync: 7 days of Slack, GDrive, Asana, GitHub in one context dump

modules.title: Terminal & Environment
modules.headline: Ghostty, statusline, vim mode, voice input, and custom spinners.
modules.subheadline: The terminal setup that makes everything smooth. Ghostty for rendering, /statusline for context tracking, /keybindings for customization, voice input for 3x faster prompting, and output styles to match your workflow.
focus: Ghostty terminal: synchronized rendering, 24-bit color, proper Unicode
/statusline: model, directory, git branch, context usage, cost, elapsed time
/keybindings: remap any key, settings live-reload immediately
/voice: hold spacebar to dictate — 3x faster, naturally more detailed prompts
Output styles: Explanatory, Learning, Custom — match Claude's voice to your workflow
/terminal-setup: fix Shift+Enter in IDE terminals, Warp, Alacritty
